items.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: as Jelly Roll Morton’s music that he recorded in Chicago “Chicago Jazz” or “New Orleans Jazz?” I don’t know.

ctx.x: Could be. I didn’t think of that. Did you notice, as long as we’re talking about that, your listening habits, could you tell a difference between New Orleans Classic Jazz and Chicago? Was there a difference in your eyes, in your ears?

That’s a tricky one because these labels sometimes are misused and misconstrued, but labels in general can cause confusion as much as they can clarify. And a lot of the music that they call “Chicago Jazz” is really New Orleans guys taking their music to Chicago and meeting guys from Chicago and from other places, and sort of a change some, it certainly changed some, but as Jelly Roll Morton’s music that he recorded in Chicago “Chicago Jazz” or “New Orleans Jazz?” I don’t know. What do you want to call it. And…

emphasis on the solos, and there was still an ensemble going on and an emphasis on ensemble but there’d be a lot more solos. I’d say if there is really one difference, that would be the major difference. But it’s a little blurred because a lot of those guys were patterning themselves after New Orleans musicians and New Orleans bands, but they’d sort of come up with their own way of doing it.
